definition_zh: 选择；选项；选择权；（金融）期权；（计算机）选项
definition_en: one of several things that can be chosen; the freedom or right to choose; a right to buy or sell something at a fixed price
core_image: 几张摊开的牌，你伸手只拿起其中一张
scene: 申请研究生时，她在纸上列出三所学校，比较学费、城市和专业方向。She wrote: Each school is one option, and I can keep all three open until the last week.
sceneCN: 这里 option 是「可供选择的方案」（第 1 个义项：可选的事物之一）；句意：每一所学校都是一个选项，我可以把这三所学校都留到最后一刻再决定。图中可辨识物件：申请表、三所学校名单、铅笔、计算器；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: One of the things you can choose
senses.definition: one of two or more things that you can choose to have or do
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个可供选择的事物中的一个
senses.example: Studying abroad is one option; staying at home is another.
senses.exampleCN: 出国留学是一种选择，留在国内是另一种选择。
senses.why: The word names the item sitting in front of the chooser. Latin optio meant 'choice' as an act; by 1885 English extended it to 'the thing that may be chosen', so the abstract act became a concrete item on a list.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指“选择”这个行为，后来指摆在选择者面前的那一项。拉丁语 optio 是“选择”；英语到 1885 年才把它扩展到“可供选择的事物”，抽象行为于是变成了清单上的具体一项。

senses.title: The freedom or right to choose
senses.definition: the power or liberty of choosing, especially when nothing is forced
senses.definitionCN: 选择的能力或自由，尤指没有被强迫时
senses.example: Employees have the option of working from home two days a week.
senses.exampleCN: 员工可以选择每周有两天在家办公。
senses.why: From c. 1600 'action of choosing' came the 1630s sense 'power or liberty of choosing'. The emphasis moves from the chosen item to the chooser's open hand: what matters is that the hand is not forced.
senses.whyCN: 从 1600 年前后的“选择行为”，发展出 1630 年代的“选择权、选择自由”。重点从被选的物件移到了选择者那只未被强迫的手。

senses.title: An extra feature you may add
senses.titleCN: 可选配置：加钱才有的附加功能
senses.definition: a feature or piece of equipment that is available only if the buyer chooses and usually pays for it
senses.definitionCN: 只有买家选择并通常额外付费才提供的功能或设备
senses.example: Air conditioning is an option on this model, not standard equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 空调是这款车型的选装配置，不是标配。
senses.why: Here the choice itself is turned into a product. The buyer's open hand is priced: you may take the extra feature or leave it, and either way the base item still works.
senses.whyCN: 这里被出售的正是“选择”本身。选择者那只张开的手被标上了价格：你可以拿这项附加功能，也可以不拿，而基础产品照样能用。

senses.title: Stock option: a right to buy shares
senses.titleCN: 股票期权：按约定价格买股份的权利
senses.definition: a right given to an employee or investor to buy company shares at a set price within a set period
senses.definitionCN: 给予员工或投资者在约定期限内按约定价格购买公司股份的权利
senses.example: The startup offered her stock options as part of the package.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司把股票期权作为薪酬方案的一部分提供给她。
senses.why: A share option is literally a purchased choice: the holder may buy at the fixed price or walk away. The 1755 commercial sense 'privilege secured by payment of a premium' is the direct ancestor of this financial use.
senses.whyCN: 股票期权字面上就是“买来的选择权”：持有人可以按固定价格买入，也可以放弃。1755 年那条“支付权利金换得的特权”的商业义，正是这一金融用法的直系祖先。

senses.title: Option contract: a right with a price
senses.titleCN: 期权合约：有价格的权利
senses.definition: a contract giving the buyer the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a stated price before a deadline
senses.definitionCN: 赋予买方在截止日期前按约定价格买入或卖出资产的权利而非义务的合约
senses.example: The fund bought an option to purchase the land at a fixed price.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金买入了按固定价格购买这块土地的选择权。
senses.why: The legal instrument isolates the core idea of the word: a choice that is bought, bounded by a price and a date. The holder pays for the open hand and may still refuse to close it.
senses.whyCN: 这种法律工具把词的核心抽离出来：一个被买下、受价格和日期约束的选择。持有人为那只张开的手付费，并且仍然可以拒绝合拢。

senses.title: The option play in football
senses.titleCN: 美式橄榄球中的“选择战术”
senses.definition: an American football play in which the ball carrier may either pass or run
senses.definitionCN: 美式橄榄球中持球者可选择传球或自己带球推进的战术
senses.example: The quarterback kept the ball on the option play.
senses.exampleCN: 四分卫在这个选择战术中自己带球推进。
senses.why: Recorded by 1953, the play gives the carrier two live choices at the moment of action. The name is not about a product or a contract but about a decision still open while the body is already moving.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法记录于 1953 年：战术让持球者在动作发生的瞬间保有两条真实可走的路线。名字说的不是产品或合约，而是身体已经动起来时仍然敞开的选择。

senses.title: A setting or flag in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的选项或参数开关
senses.definition: a selectable setting, flag, or argument that changes how a program behaves
senses.definitionCN: 改变程序行为方式的可选设置、开关或参数
senses.example: Add the -v option to see verbose output.
senses.exampleCN: 加上 -v 选项即可查看详细输出。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the everyday sense: a program offers a menu of behaviours, and the user picks one. The choice is now made by typing a flag rather than by pointing at a card.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域借用了日常义：程序把若干行为列成菜单，用户挑一个。选择方式从“指着卡片”变成了“敲一个参数”。

senses.title: Keeping alternatives available
senses.titleCN: 保留余地：让选择继续敞开
senses.definition: in the phrase keep options open, to avoid committing so that alternatives stay available
senses.definitionCN: 用于 keep options open，表示不做出承诺，以便保留其他可能
senses.example: She kept her options open by applying to several programs.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了好几个项目，以此保留选择余地。
senses.why: This phrase makes the open hand visible. Not choosing yet is itself a choice, because the alternatives remain graspable and no single card has been lifted from the table.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语让“张开的手”变得可见。暂不选择本身也是一种选择：其他可能仍然可抓，桌上没有哪张牌被真正拿走。

intro.en: Option comes from Latin through French. The date of the English noun is clear; the origin of the Latin verb optare is not, and standard references mark it as uncertain.
intro.cn: option 经由法语来自拉丁语。英语名词的年代清楚，但拉丁动词 optare 的来源并不清楚，通行资料标注为不确定。

items.en: c. 1600, 'action of choosing'; by the 1630s, 'power or liberty of choosing'. The noun entered English through French option (Old French opcion).
items.cn: 约 1600 年记录为“选择的行为”；到 1630 年代为“选择的能力或自由”。名词经法语 option（古法语 opcion）进入英语。

items.en: From Latin optionem (nominative optio) 'choice, free choice, liberty to choose', a noun from optare 'to desire, pray for, choose'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 optionem（主格 optio）“选择、自由选择、选择的自由”，是由 optare“渴望、祈求、选择”构成的名词。

items.en: De Vaan derives optare from Proto-Italic *opeje- 'to choose, grab', from PIE *hopeie-, and compares Hittite epp-/app- 'to take, grab'. This deeper reconstruction is debated, so the ultimate root is source uncertain.
items.cn: De Vaan 把 optare 追溯到原始意大利语 *opeje-“选择、抓取”，再往上到原始印欧语 *hopeie-，并与赫梯语 epp-/app-“拿、抓”比较。这一更深层重构仍有争议，故最底层词源来源不确定。

items.en: 1755 records the commercial sense 'privilege secured by payment of a premium'; 1885 records 'thing that may be chosen'. The word thus moved from act to right to object.
items.cn: 1755 年记录商业义“支付权利金换得的特权”；1885 年记录“可供选择的事物”。词义由此从行为走到权利，再走到物件。

items.en: 1953 records the football option play. The computing sense of a selectable flag is a later 20c. extension of the everyday 'choice' meaning.
items.cn: 1953 年记录橄榄球的 option play（选择战术）。计算机中“可选开关”的义项是 20 世纪后期由日常“选择”义扩展而来。

note.en: The first group separates words that merely look like option; the second compares words that really mean a choice.
note.cn: 第一组只把外形相近的词分开；第二组比较真正表示“选择”的词。

entries.definition: a process or set of actions, especially in surgery or business. It starts with op- but comes from Latin opus 'work', not optare.
entries.definitionCN: 操作；手术；业务。它同样以 op- 开头，但来自拉丁语 opus“工作”，而不是 optare。

entries.definition: a belief or judgment not fully proved. It is linked in dictionaries to opinari 'to think', whose own origin is unknown, and is not a form of option.
entries.definitionCN: 意见；看法。词典把它连到 opinari“认为”，而 opinari 本身来源不明，它不是 option 的变形。

entries.definition: relating to light or the eyes. Its opt- goes back to Greek optos 'seen', a different root from Latin optare.
entries.definitionCN: 光学的；视觉的。它的 opt- 来自希腊语 optos“被看见的”，与拉丁语 optare 是不同的词根。

entries.definition: in grammar, a mood that expresses a wish. It is built directly on Latin optare 'to wish', so it is a true relative of option.
entries.definitionCN: 语法中的祈愿语气。它直接由拉丁语 optare“希望”构成，因此是 option 的真正同族词。

entries.definition: the act of choosing, or the range of things from which one may choose. It is the everyday word; option is more formal and often implies a listed alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 选择的行为，或可供选择的整体范围。它是最日常的词；option 更正式，常指清单上列出的一个备选。

entries.definition: one of two or more possibilities that can replace each other. It stresses replacement; option stresses that the thing is available to pick.
entries.definitionCN: 两个或多个可相互替代的可能之一。它强调“替换”，option 强调“可供挑选”。

entries.definition: the act of selecting, or the set of things chosen. It often refers to a curated range rather than a single item.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选的行为，或被挑出的一组事物。它常指经过整理的一组，而不是单个选项。

entries.definition: a stronger liking for one thing over another. It names the ranking in the chooser's mind, not the item itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物更强的偏好。它指选择者心里的排序，而不是被选的那个事物。

normalIntro.en: Five sound-and-spelling hooks, then three abstract images for the idea behind the word.
normalIntro.cn: 先给五个读音与拼写挂钩，再用三个抽象画面记住这个词背后的观念。

normal.en: op- sounds like 'open': an option is a door left open until you walk through one.
normal.cn: op- 听起来像 open（打开）：option 就是一扇直到你走进某一间之前都开着的门。

normal.en: -tion marks an action, as in action: choosing is something you do, not a thing that happens to you.
normal.cn: -tion 像 action 里的那个 -tion，标记“动作”：选择是你做的事，不是落到你身上的事。

normal.en: opt out is 'choose out', opt in is 'choose in': the same root with opposite directions.
normal.cn: opt out 是“选出去”（退出），opt in 是“选进来”（加入）：同一个词根，方向相反。

normal.en: Keep options open = keep the cards on the table, not in your pocket.
normal.cn: keep options open＝把牌留在桌上，而不是揣进口袋。

normal.en: optional ends in -al like 'additional': an optional extra is one you may add.
normal.cn: optional 和 additional 一样以 -al 结尾：optional extra 就是你可以“加”的那一项。

abstract.en: An option is the smallest unit of freedom: a real alternative that you can still take.
abstract.cn: 选项是自由的最小单位：一个你仍然拿得走的真实备选。

abstract.en: Every option is a road not yet walked; choosing burns the other roads for this trip.
abstract.cn: 每个选项都是一条尚未走过的路；一旦选择，这一趟的其他路就被烧掉了。

abstract.en: A financial option puts a price on possibility itself: you pay to keep a choice alive.
abstract.cn: 金融期权给“可能性”本身标了价：你付钱，只为让一个选择继续活着。

examples.en: The report lists several options for cutting costs, but none is painless.
examples.cn: 报告列出了几种削减成本的选项，但没有一种是轻松的。

examples.en: You always have the option to say no.
examples.cn: 你始终拥有拒绝的选项。

examples.en: The software hides advanced options unless you open the settings panel.
examples.cn: 除非打开设置面板，否则软件会隐藏高级选项。

dict_mnemonic.note: 把 opt- 记成“伸手抓取”，-ion 记成“动作”：抓取的动作就是选择。
dict_mnemonic.text: opt（抓取、选择）+ -ion（名词）→ 选择、选项、选择权

root: 拉丁 optare“希望、选择”→ optio“选择”→ 法语 option → 英语 option；更早的原始印欧来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from 'a thing you may pick' to 'the right to pick', then to priced choices (features, stock, contracts), and finally to a live choice inside a game, a program, or a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“可供挑选的事物”走到“挑选的权利”，再到被标价的选择（选装配置、股票、合约），最后落到比赛、程序与计划中仍然敞开的那一次选择。

core.en: An open hand above several alternatives, ready to lift one
core.cn: 悬在几个备选之上的手，随时准备拿起一个

branches.en: Concrete alternatives: one item on a list of things you may pick.
branches.cn: 具体备选：可供挑选的清单上的一项。

branches.en: Freedom kept open: the chooser's liberty, or the deliberate refusal to commit.
branches.cn: 被保留的自由：选择者的权利，或有意不作承诺。

branches.en: Choices sold as goods: an add-on feature or a stock option.
branches.cn: 作为商品出售的选择：选装配置或股票期权。

branches.en: Choices inside a system: a football play or a software flag.
branches.cn: 系统内部的选择：橄榄球战术或软件开关。

branches.en: The paid right: liberty turned into a priced, time-limited contract.
branches.cn: 付费的权利：自由变成有价格、有期限的合约。

intro.en: The opt- family is small but busy: a verb of choosing, a noun of choice, and adjectives that mark whether something is left to the chooser.
intro.cn: opt- 词族不大但很活跃：一个“选择”动词、一个“选择”名词，以及标记“是否交由选择者决定”的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin optare 'to wish, choose' yields optio 'choice' and the adjective optativus 'expressing a wish'. English opt is a back-formation from option.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 optare“希望、选择”产生 optio“选择”和形容词 optativus“表达愿望的”。英语的 opt 是从 option 逆构出来的动词。

items.meaning: the act or right of choosing; a thing chosen
items.meaningCN: 选择的行为或权利；被选中的事物
items.example: You have the option to decline.
Attendance is optional.

items.meaning: in a way that is not required
items.example: The form can optionally include a photo.
items.exampleCN: 表格可以选择附上一张照片。

items.meaning: to choose or decide between alternatives
items.example: Most students opt for the shorter course.
items.exampleCN: 大多数学生选择较短的那门课。

items.meaning: a choice to leave or not take part
items.example: The newsletter uses an opt-out system.
items.exampleCN: 这份通讯采用“默认订阅、可退出”的机制。

items.meaning: a choice to join or take part
items.example: Marketing emails require opt-in consent.
items.exampleCN: 营销邮件需要用户主动选择加入的同意。

items.meaning: to choose for oneself and take as one's own
items.meaningCN: 采纳；收养（选择过来成为自己的）
items.example: The school adopted a new reading method.
items.exampleCN: 学校采纳了一种新的阅读教学法。

items.meaning: the act of taking something as one's own
items.example: The adoption of the plan took two years.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划的采纳用了两年。

items.meaning: expressing a wish, as a grammatical mood
items.example: Ancient Greek has an optative mood.

latinEntries.example: Latin optare aliquid means to wish for something.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 optare aliquid 意为“渴望某物”。

latinEntries.meaning: choice, free choice, liberty to choose
latinEntries.meaningCN: 选择、自由选择、选择的自由
latinEntries.example: Optio is the source of French option.
latinEntries.exampleCN: optio 是法语 option 的来源。

latinEntries.meaning: to choose for oneself, take by choice
latinEntries.meaningCN: 为自己挑选；选择并接纳
latinEntries.example: Adoptare is the source of English adopt.
latinEntries.exampleCN: adoptare 是英语 adopt 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Optativus modus is the wishing mood.

definition_en: the arrangement of things in a sequence, a command, or a rank in biological classification
core_image: 一队人按身高排成一行，队首的人手里拿着写有编号的名单
scene: 火车站的值班员按出发时间把列车排成一条队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次。 At the station the dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure, and passengers followed that sequence to find their own service.
sceneCN: 这里 order 是「顺序、次序」（第 1 个义项：事物按先后排列的方式）；句意：值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 顺序；次序；秩序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；修会；勋章

senses.title: A sequence of things
senses.definition: the way things are arranged one after another, especially according to time, size or importance
senses.definitionCN: 事物按时间、大小或重要性一个接一个排列的方式
senses.example: The dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure.
senses.exampleCN: 值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列。
senses.why: Latin ordo first meant a row of threads in a loom, then a row of any kind; a sequence is literally a row read from one end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 ordo 最初指织机上一排经线，后指任何一排；所谓顺序，字面上就是从一端读过去的一排。

senses.title: A command given to someone
senses.definition: an instruction that must be obeyed, especially one given by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 必须服从的指示，尤指由权威给出的指示
senses.example: The captain gave the order to close the gates.
senses.exampleCN: 队长下令关闭大门。
senses.why: A command is what puts others into an order: the word names both the arrangement and the act of imposing it, which is why a military order and a neat row share one term.
senses.whyCN: 命令就是让别人进入某种次序：这个词既指排列，也指强加排列的动作，因此军令与整齐的一行共用一个词。

senses.title: A purchase request
senses.definition: a request for goods or food to be supplied, or the goods so requested
senses.definitionCN: 要求供应商品或食物的请求，或如此要求的货物
senses.example: She placed an order for two hundred copies.
senses.exampleCN: 她订购了两百册。
senses.why: Commerce extended the word from arrangement to instruction: an order tells a supplier what to arrange and in what quantity.
senses.whyCN: 商业把这个词从排列延伸到指示：订单告诉供货者要安排什么、数量多少。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank order
senses.definition: the rank below class and above family in biological classification
senses.definitionCN: 生物分类中位于纲之下、科之上的阶元
senses.example: The order contains twelve families of beetles.
senses.exampleCN: 这个目包含十二个甲虫科。
senses.why: Taxonomy used the Latin word for a row: an order is a row of families, read in one direction down the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 分类学用了这个意为「一排」的拉丁词：一个目就是一排科，沿层级往一个方向读下去。

senses.title: Social or public order
senses.definition: the condition in which rules are obeyed and normal activity can continue
senses.definitionCN: 规则得到遵守、正常活动得以继续的状态
senses.example: The police restored order after the march.
senses.exampleCN: 游行之后警方恢复了秩序。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the row: when everyone is in their place, the whole is in order, and the word names that condition rather than any particular row.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「一排」一般化：当人人各在其位，整体就有秩序，这个词命名的正是那种状态，而非某一特定行列。

senses.title: A religious order
senses.definition: a body of monks, nuns or friars living under one rule, such as the Franciscans
senses.definitionCN: 遵同一会规生活的修士、修女或托钵僧团体，如方济各会
senses.example: The order ran the hospital for three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修会经营了那所医院三百年。
senses.why: A religious order is a body ordered by a rule; the word names both the community and the discipline that holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 修会是一个按会规排序的团体；这个词既指群体，也指维系群体的那套纪律。

senses.title: An honorary order or decoration
senses.definition: a society of people honoured for service, or the decoration that marks membership
senses.definitionCN: 因功绩受表彰者组成的团体，或标记成员身份的勋章
senses.example: He was admitted to the order for public service.
senses.exampleCN: 他因公共服务被授予该勋位。
senses.why: The sense grew from rank: an order is a graded body of members, and the medal is the visible mark of one's place in it.
senses.whyCN: 这一义由「等级」生长出来：勋位是一个分级的成员团体，勋章则是个人在其中的位置可见的标记。

senses.title: A procedural point in a meeting
senses.definition: a question raised about whether the rules of procedure are being followed, as in a point of order
senses.definitionCN: 关于议事规则是否得到遵守而提出的问题，如程序问题
senses.example: A member raised a point of order before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 表决之前有成员提出了程序问题。
senses.why: Meetings run by rules, and the rules are themselves an order; raising a point of order is asking whether the meeting is still following its own arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 会议依规则进行，而规则本身即是一种秩序；提出程序问题就是问会议是否仍遵守自己的安排。

senses.title: Order of magnitude
senses.definition: a class of scale in which one value is about ten times another, used for rough comparison
senses.definitionCN: 一个值约为另一个值的十倍的尺度等级，用于粗略比较
senses.example: The cost rose by an order of magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 成本上升了一个数量级。
senses.why: Here order is a step in a graded series: each step multiplies by ten, so the word names a rung rather than a sequence of items.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 order 是分级系列中的一级：每一级乘以十，因此这个词命名的是一级台阶，而不是一串物件。

senses.title: The classical orders of architecture
senses.definition: one of the recognized styles of column and entablature, such as Doric or Corinthian
senses.definitionCN: 多立克、科林斯等被承认的柱与檐部样式之一
senses.example: The facade mixes two architectural orders on one level.
senses.exampleCN: 这面外墙在同一层混用了两种柱式。
senses.why: Vitruvius used ordo for the due arrangement of parts, and the word became the name of each fixed arrangement of column and capital.
senses.whyCN: 维特鲁威用 ordo 指各部分的合宜安排，这个词后来成为柱与柱头每一种固定搭配的名称。

intro.en: Order comes from Latin ordo 'row, rank, arrangement', a third-declension noun whose deeper origin is disputed. It entered English through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: order 来自拉丁 ordo「一排、等级、安排」，是第三变格法名词，其更深来源有争议。该词经古法语进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, especially a row of threads in a loom, then a rank or an arrangement. The physical row is the oldest image.
items.cn: ordo 指一排，尤其织机上的一排经线，后指等级或安排。物理的一排是最古老的意象。

items.en: The noun is linked to ordiri 'to begin, to lay out a warp'; the connection is accepted, though the verb's own origin is debated.
items.cn: 该名词与 ordiri「开始、铺开经线」相关；这一联系一般认为是成立的，但动词本身的来源仍有争论。

items.en: Old French ordre brought the word into English, where it covered both a row and a command by the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 ordre 把该词带入英语，到 13 世纪已兼指一排与命令。

items.en: The medieval church used order for the ranks of clergy, and the phrase religious order fixed the sense of a community under one rule.
items.cn: 中世纪教会用 order 指神职等级，religious order 一语则固定了「同一会规下的团体」这一义。

items.en: Linnaeus gave order a place in his hierarchy in the eighteenth century, between class and family.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪给 order 在层级中安排了位置，位于纲与科之间。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between ordo and ordiri is generally accepted, but the pre-Latin origin of both is unsettled, so Indo-European forms offered for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ordo 与 ordiri 的联系一般认为是成立的，但二者在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates the many English words that descend from ordo; group two compares words of neighbouring meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分源自 ordo 的众多英语词；第二组比较意思相邻的词。

entries.definition: A number that marks position in a series, such as first or tenth, from ordinalis. It names a place, not a command.
entries.definitionCN: 标记序列位置的数词，如第一、第十，出自 ordinalis。它指位置，不指命令。

entries.definition: Common or usual, from ordinarius 'according to order'. The sense drifted from 'regular' to 'unremarkable'.
entries.definitionCN: 普通、通常的，出自 ordinarius「按次序的」。词义从「合规矩」漂移到「不出奇」。

entries.definition: A decree or regulation, from ordinare 'to arrange'. It is a law that arranges conduct, not a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 法令或条例，出自 ordinare「安排」。它是安排行为的法规，不是顺序。

entries.definition: To confer holy orders or to decree, from ordinare. It names an authoritative act, not an arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 授予圣职或颁布，出自 ordinare。它指权威性的行为，而非排列。

entries.definition: A series in which one thing follows another, from sequi 'to follow'. It stresses succession, while order can also mean a command or a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 一物接一物形成的系列，出自 sequi「跟随」。它强调接续，而 order 还可指命令或阶元。

entries.definition: The way items are placed relative to one another. It is the result, while order can be the principle behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 各物彼此的摆放方式。它是结果，order 则可以是背后的原则。

entries.definition: A directive from an authority. It matches one branch of order but not the sequence branch.
entries.definitionCN: 权威发出的指示。它对应 order 的一支，而不对应顺序那一支。

entries.definition: A position in a graded scale, as in taxonomic rank. It names the level, while order can name the whole arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 分级尺度中的位置，如分类阶元。它指层级，order 则可指整套安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ordo was a row of threads: order is first a row, then a rule that keeps things in rows.
normal.cn: ordo 原是一排经线：order 先是一排，后指使事物各在其排的规则。

normal.en: The same word gives ordinal, ordinary, ordinance and ordain, all built on ordinare 'to arrange'.
normal.cn: 同一个词给出 ordinal、ordinary、ordinance、ordain，皆基于 ordinare「安排」。

normal.en: In biology the order sits between class and family, one rung of the ladder.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，目位于纲与科之间，是梯子上的一级。

normal.en: A point of order asks whether the meeting is following its own rules.
normal.cn: 程序问题问的是会议是否遵守自己的规则。

normal.en: An order of magnitude is one step of ten, a rung rather than a row.
normal.cn: 数量级是以十为一步的一级，是一级台阶而非一排。

abstract.en: Picture a loom where one wrong thread makes the whole pattern shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一台织机，一根线错了，整个花样就移位。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that stays calm because everyone knows their number.
abstract.cn: 想象一支队伍因为人人知道自己的号而保持平静。

abstract.en: Picture a cabinet whose drawers are labelled by size, each ten times the one before.
abstract.cn: 想象一柜按大小标注的抽屉，每一格是前一格的十倍。

examples.en: The names were read out in the order in which they had been received.
examples.cn: 姓名按收到的先后顺序被念出。

examples.en: The general's order reached the front line before dawn.
examples.cn: 将军的命令在黎明前传到了前线。

examples.en: The two families belong to the same order but different superfamilies.
examples.cn: 这两个科属于同一个目，但属于不同的总科。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「or 或者 + der 得」——或者这样排、或者那样排，总得有个次序 → order 顺序；命令

root: 拉丁 ordo, ordinis「一排、等级、安排」，与 ordiri「铺开经线、开始」相关；更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of order follow the row outward: a sequence, a command that imposes sequence, a purchase, a taxonomic rung, social calm, a ruled community, an honour, a procedural question, a factor of ten and a style of columns.
sensesIntro.cn: order 的十个义项沿着「一排」向外走：顺序、强加顺序的命令、订单、生物阶元、社会安定、守会规的团体、勋位、程序问题、十倍一级、柱式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row read from one end, and the rule that keeps it a row.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一端读过去的一排，以及使它保持成一排的那条规则。

branches.en: THE ROW ITSELF: a sequence of items, a factor of ten, or a fixed arrangement of columns.
branches.cn: 一排本身：一串物件、十倍的级差，或柱子的固定搭配。

branches.en: THE INSTRUCTION: a command and a purchase both tell someone what to arrange.
branches.cn: 指示：命令与订单都在告诉别人该安排什么。

branches.en: THE RANK: an order in taxonomy and an honour both place a member on a graded ladder.
branches.cn: 等级：生物学的目与勋位都把成员放在分级的梯子上。

branches.en: THE RULE: social order and a point of order both concern whether rules are being kept.
branches.cn: 规则：社会秩序与程序问题都关心规则是否被遵守。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY: a religious order is a body held together by one rule.
branches.cn: 团体：修会是由一条会规维系的群体。

intro.en: Order is a Latin noun that English uses for rows, commands and ranks alike; the common thread is arranged position.
intro.cn: order 是拉丁名词，英语用它同时指行列、命令与等级；共同的线索是「被安排的位置」。

latinIntro.en: Latin ordo yields order, ordinal, ordinary, ordinance and ordain; ordinare 'to arrange' is the verb behind the derived forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ordo 衍生 order、ordinal、ordinary、ordinance、ordain；ordinare「安排」是这些派生形式背后的动词。

items.example: Ordo began as a row of threads.
The verb supplies ordering and ordinance.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 ordering 与 ordinance。

items.example: One word covers the row and the rule.
items.exampleCN: 一个词同时覆盖一排与规则。

items.example: Ordinal numbers answer 'which place'.
The ordinary sense drifted to 'unremarkable'.
items.exampleCN: ordinary 的词义漂移到「不出奇」。

items.example: An ordinance arranges conduct by rule.
Ordain names the act of putting someone in place.
items.exampleCN: ordain 指把某人放到位置上的行为。

items.example: An orderly ward keeps everything in its row.
items.exampleCN: 整齐的病房让一切各在其位。

items.example: A suborder narrows the row of families.

definition_zh: 普通的；平常的；平凡的；例行的
definition_en: normal and not special or unusual; plain and not impressive; and also fixed by rule or custom as the standard course
core_image: 一条街上并排的店门，招牌颜色都差不多，没人多看一眼
scene: 下班时分的街上，人流照常往车站走，谁也没注意招牌换了新灯。It was an ordinary evening until the rain began.
sceneCN: 这里是「普通的、平常的」（第 1 个义项：没有特别之处）；句意为直到下雨之前，那都是个平常的傍晚。图中可辨识物件：并排的店门、招牌、往车站去的人流。

pos.zh: 普通的；平常的；平凡的；例行的

derivatives.zh: 由 ordinary 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「通常地；一般地」
由 ordinary 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「平凡；普通」
由前缀 extra-（在……之外）加 ordinary 构成，义为「非凡的；异常的」

senses.title: Not special or unusual
senses.definition: normal and not special, unusual or different from other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 正常的，与同类事物相比没有特别、奇特或不同之处
senses.example: He ordered an ordinary coffee and sat by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他点了一杯普通咖啡，坐在窗边。
senses.why: The Latin adjective ordinarius described what follows the regular order of things, so the ordinary is whatever fits the usual pattern.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词 ordinarius 形容「按事物常规次序来的东西」，所以 ordinary 就是老老实实符合平常样子的那一个。

senses.title: Not impressive or remarkable
senses.definition: plain and not especially good, talented or interesting
senses.definitionCN: 平实无奇，谈不上出色、有才或有意思
senses.example: It was a perfectly ordinary performance, neither bad nor memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一场再平凡不过的演出，不算差，也不值得记住。
senses.why: If something merely follows the usual order, it has nothing that lifts it above the line, and that absence becomes the sense of being unremarkable.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西只是照着常规次序排进去，就没有任何地方把它抬出那条线；这种「没有高出来」的缺位，就成了「不出众」的意思。

senses.title: Established and routine
senses.definition: fixed by rule or custom and regularly followed, as in ordinary business or an ordinary session
senses.definitionCN: 按规章或惯例定下来、定期照办的，如常规业务或例会
senses.example: The committee meets on ordinary business twice a month.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会每月就常规事务开两次会。
senses.why: In law and administration an ordinary procedure is the one laid down as the standard course, so the word also names what is done by rule rather than by exception.
senses.whyCN: 在法律与行政里，ordinary 程序指被规定为标准做法的那一套，所以这个词也用来指照规章办、而非特例的事情。

intro.en: Ordinary comes from the Latin adjective for what follows the usual order, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: ordinary 来自拉丁语中表示「按常规次序」的形容词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Ordo meant a row or a fixed arrangement, and it is the root of the whole family, including order and ordinary.
items.cn: ordo 指一排或固定的次序，是整个词族的根，包括 order 与 ordinary。

items.en: Ordinarius meant according to the usual order, regular or standard, as opposed to what is exceptional.
items.cn: ordinarius 意为「按通常次序的、正规的、标准的」，与例外相对。

items.en: Old French ordinaire kept the sense of usual and customary, and it supplied the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语的 ordinaire 保留「通常、惯常」的意思，英语借用的正是这个形式。

items.en: Early English ordinary meant customary or usual, and the word was also a noun for an official with regular jurisdiction.
items.cn: 早期英语的 ordinary 意为「惯常的、通常的」，同时也可作名词，指拥有常规管辖权的官员。

items.en: Modern English widened it to everyday things and people, adding the weaker sense of being plain or unremarkable.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到日常事物与普通人，并添上「平实、不出众」这层较弱的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ordinary family and its negated relative; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for what is common and unremarkable.
note.cn: 形近组是 ordinary 词族及其否定形式；近义组是表示「常见、不出奇」的形容词。

entries.definition: Usually, in most cases.
entries.definitionCN: 通常；在多数情况下。

entries.definition: The quality of being plain or usual.
entries.definitionCN: 平凡、普通的性质。

entries.definition: Very unusual, remarkable or far beyond the normal.
entries.definitionCN: 极不寻常的、非凡的，远超常规的。

entries.definition: Happening often or found in many places.
entries.definitionCN: 经常发生或到处可见的。

entries.definition: Happening or done most of the time.
entries.definitionCN: 多数时候会发生或去做的。

entries.definition: Simple, without decoration or special features.
entries.definitionCN: 简单、没有装饰或特别之处的。

normalIntro.en: The word carries the Latin idea of a regular row, so the mnemonics keep the picture of something placed neatly in the usual line.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「排成一行」的观念，所以联想都围绕「按平常那一行排好」的画面。

normal.en: Ordinary and order share the Latin stem ordo, a row: ordinary means staying in the usual row.
normal.cn: ordinary 与 order 共享拉丁词干 ordo（一排）：ordinary 就是留在平常那一行里。

normal.en: Ordinarily adds -ly and turns the adjective into the adverb for usually.
normal.cn: ordinarily 加 -ly，把形容词变成表示「通常」的副词。

normal.en: Ordinariness adds -ness and names the plain quality itself.
normal.cn: ordinariness 加 -ness，直接指「普通」这种性质。

normal.en: Extraordinary adds extra-, meaning outside, so it means outside the ordinary row.
normal.cn: extraordinary 加 extra-（在……之外），所以意思是「在平常那一行之外」。

normal.en: Out of the ordinary is the fixed phrase for anything unusual.
normal.cn: out of the ordinary 是表示「不寻常」的固定说法。

abstract.en: A street of shop fronts with almost the same colour: nothing asks to be looked at.
abstract.cn: 一条街的店门颜色几乎一样：没有任何一处要求你多看它一眼。

abstract.en: The word for being in the usual row is also the word for being unremarkable.
abstract.cn: 「待在平常那一行」这个词，同时就是「不出众」这个词。

abstract.en: What is ordinary today can become invisible, which is why it takes rain to make an evening noticed.
abstract.cn: 今天平常的东西会变得看不见，所以要下一场雨，一个傍晚才被注意到。

examples.en: He ordered an ordinary coffee and sat by the window.
examples.cn: 他点了一杯普通咖啡，坐在窗边。

examples.en: It was a perfectly ordinary performance, neither bad nor memorable.
examples.cn: 那是一场再平凡不过的演出，不算差，也不值得记住。

examples.en: The committee meets on ordinary business twice a month.
examples.cn: 委员会每月就常规事务开两次会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥丁纳瑞」——按着老规矩排好的那一格，谁也不会多看一眼；记住 ordinary 是普通的。

root: 拉丁语 ordo（一排、次序，属格 ordinis）派生的形容词 ordinarius（按常规次序的），经古法语 ordinaire 进入英语；ordinary 本义「照常规的」，后引申为「普通的、平凡的」。同族词有 ordinarily、extraordinary。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the usual row of things; the senses divide into what is not special, what is not impressive, and what is fixed as the standard routine.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「事物平常排成的那一行」；义项分成没有特别之处、不出众，以及被规定为标准做法三层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street of shop fronts in nearly the same colour, with no sign trying to stand out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上颜色几乎相同的店门，没有一块招牌特意跳出来。

branches.en: identical shop fronts along a street
branches.cn: 一条街上彼此相似的店门

branches.en: a man ordering the same coffee as every morning
branches.cn: 一个人点着和每个早晨一样的咖啡

branches.en: a performance that leaves no line in memory
branches.cn: 一场没在记忆里留下痕迹的演出

branches.en: a committee following its printed agenda
branches.cn: 委员会照着印好的议程开会

branches.en: a form filled in the standard way
branches.cn: 一张按标准方式填写的表格

intro.en: The word joins a Latin adjective of regular order to English suffixes, and its family adds the adverb, the noun and the negated form.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示「常规次序」的拉丁形容词接到英语后缀上，词族里再加出副词、名词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family behind ordinary is the ordo family: the noun for a row, its genitive, and the adjective ordinarius.
latinIntro.cn: ordinary 背后的拉丁词族是 ordo 一族：表示一排的名词、它的属格，以及形容词 ordinarius。

definition_zh: 器官；管风琴；机构；喉舌；工具
definition_en: a part of a living body that performs a special function, or an instrument, body or publication that serves a particular purpose
core_image: 一台有专门职责的装置，嵌在更大的机器里，各自完成一道工序
scene: 医院走廊的指示牌上画着人体轮廓，每个部位旁标注它负责的功能： Each organ in the abdomen has its own job.
sceneCN: 这里指「生物器官」（第 1 个义项：执行特定功能的独立身体部件）；句意为腹腔里的每个器官都有各自的分工；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 器官（身体中执行特定功能的部分）
管风琴；机构；机关报刊；喉舌

senses.title: Body organ
senses.titleCN: 生物器官：执行特定功能的部件
senses.definition: a part of an animal or plant body made of several tissues and carrying out a special job
senses.definitionCN: 由多种组织构成、承担特定功能的动物或植物身体部件
senses.example: Each organ in the abdomen has its own job.
senses.exampleCN: 腹腔里的每个器官都有自己的职责。
senses.why: The oldest anatomical sense treats the body as a machine with distinct working parts, each named for its task.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的解剖义把身体当作一台有明确工作部件的机器，每个部件按任务命名。

senses.title: Pipe organ
senses.titleCN: 管风琴：由多组音管构成的乐器
senses.definition: a large musical instrument in which air is forced through pipes to produce sound
senses.definitionCN: 让气流通过音管发声的大型乐器
senses.example: The cathedral organ filled the hall with sound.
senses.exampleCN: 教堂的管风琴让整个大厅充满声音。
senses.why: The instrument is a set of pipes each doing one job, so the body-part word was applied to a machine made of specialised parts.
senses.whyCN: 这件乐器是一组各司其职的音管，于是「身体部件」这个词被用到由专门部件构成的机器上。

senses.title: Government body
senses.definition: an official institution that carries out a particular public function
senses.definitionCN: 承担某项公共职能的官方机构
senses.example: The central bank is an organ of the state, not a private company.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行是国家机关，不是私人公司。
senses.why: An institution is a working part of the state in the same way an organ is a working part of a body.
senses.whyCN: 机构是国家的执行部件，正如器官是身体的执行部件。

senses.title: Party newspaper
senses.definition: a newspaper or magazine that speaks officially for a party, union or movement
senses.definitionCN: 代表政党、工会或运动正式发声的报纸或杂志
senses.example: The party's official organ published the speech in full.
senses.exampleCN: 该党的机关报全文刊登了这篇讲话。
senses.why: A publication becomes the mouth of an organization, so the body-part word shifts from doing work to speaking for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 出版物成为组织的嘴，于是这个身体部件词从「执行工作」转为「替整体发声」。

senses.title: Vocal organs
senses.definition: the parts of the body, such as the larynx and vocal cords, used to produce voice
senses.definitionCN: 喉、声带等用于产生声音的身体部件
senses.example: Damage to the vocal organs can change a singer's range.
senses.exampleCN: 发声器官受损会改变歌手的音域。
senses.why: Speech is a bodily function, so the parts that produce it are organs in the strict anatomical sense.
senses.whyCN: 言语是一种身体功能，产生它的部件按严格解剖义就是器官。

senses.title: Sense organ
senses.definition: a structure such as the eye or ear that receives a particular kind of stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 眼、耳等接收特定刺激的结构
senses.example: The eye is a sense organ tuned to light.
senses.exampleCN: 眼睛是对光敏感的感觉器官。
senses.why: Each sense has a dedicated receiver, and a dedicated working part is exactly what the word organ names.
senses.whyCN: 每种感觉都有专门的接收器，而「专门的执行部件」正是这个词所指。

senses.title: Reproductive organ
senses.definition: a structure that produces or carries sex cells, such as the flower of a plant
senses.definitionCN: 产生或承载生殖细胞的结构，如植物的花
senses.example: The flower is the reproductive organ of the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 花是植物的繁殖器官。
senses.why: The botanical use extends the anatomical word to plants, where a flower is the dedicated part for one function.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把这个解剖词扩展到植物：花就是专司一项功能的部件。

senses.title: Instrument or means, archaic
senses.definition: an instrument or means by which something is done, the oldest general sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 用来做某事的工具或手段，是该词最古老的泛义
senses.example: In old texts, a pen is called the organ of the writer.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老文本里，笔被称为书写者的工具。
senses.why: Greek organon meant any tool, so English once used organ for instruments in general before the body and music senses took over.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语这个词泛指任何工具，因此英语早期曾用它泛指器具，后来才被身体义与音乐义占据。

intro.en: Organ comes from Latin organum, borrowed from Greek organon, a tool or instrument, which is generally connected with Greek ergon work. The musical and bodily senses developed separately. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organ 来自拉丁 organum，借自希腊 organon「工具、器具」，一般认为与希腊 ergon「工作」有关。音乐义与身体义各自独立发展。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek organon meant a tool, implement or instrument, including a musical instrument and, in medical writing, a part of the body.
items.cn: 希腊 organon 意为工具、器具或乐器，在医学写作中也指身体的一部分。

items.en: The usual account connects organon with ergon work, so a tool is what does work; the Indo-European root behind ergon is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 通行解释把 organon 与 ergon「工作」联系起来，即工具就是干活的东西；ergon 背后的印欧词根属重构形式。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument, engine or musical instrument, and used it in translations of Greek medical texts.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum，指器具、器械或乐器，并在翻译希腊医学文献时使用它。

items.en: The church organ gave the word its everyday musical sense in medieval English, where organ meant the instrument before it meant the body part.
items.cn: 教堂管风琴让这个词在中古英语中获得日常音乐义：在指身体部件之前，organ 先指这件乐器。

items.en: The body sense was revived through medical Latin in the sixteenth century and then spread to every part with a special function.
items.cn: 身体义在 16 世纪经医学拉丁语重新兴起，随后扩展到每一个有专门功能的部件。

items.en: The sense of an official body or newspaper developed from the older idea of an instrument or mouthpiece; the exact dates of each branch are uncertain.
items.cn: 官方机构或机关报的义项由更早的「工具、喉舌」观念发展而来；各支线确切的年代存疑。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on organ; the second holds body parts and general words that are often swapped for it.
note.cn: 第一组是由 organ 构成的同根形式；第二组是常与它替换的身体部件词与泛用词。

entries.definition: A specialised structure inside a cell; the suffix -elle makes it a little organ, smaller than an organ.
entries.definitionCN: 细胞内的专门结构；后缀 -elle 使它成为「小器官」，比器官更小。

entries.definition: A whole living being, not one of its parts; the suffix -ism marks the total body.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的活体，而非其中一个部件；后缀 -ism 标记整体。

entries.definition: Relating to organs or to living things; it describes and cannot stand for the noun organ.
entries.definitionCN: 与器官或生物有关的；它是描述词，不能代替名词 organ。

entries.definition: The Latin noun behind organ, still used in historical music writing for early polyphony.
entries.definitionCN: organ 背后的拉丁名词，在音乐史写作中仍指早期复调。

entries.definition: A layer of similar cells; organs are built from several tissues, so tissue is the material and organ the working unit.
entries.definitionCN: 相似细胞构成的一层；器官由多种组织建成，因此组织是材料，器官是工作单位。

entries.definition: An organ that makes and releases a substance; it is one kind of organ, not a synonym for all organs.
entries.definitionCN: 制造并释放物质的器官；它是器官的一种，并非所有器官的同义词。

entries.definition: An arm, leg or wing; a limb is an appendage, while an organ is an internal working part.
entries.definitionCN: 臂、腿或翼；肢体是附肢，而器官是内部执行部件。

entries.definition: Any tool or means, including a musical instrument; it overlaps the oldest sense of organ but lacks the body sense.
entries.definitionCN: 任何工具或手段，包括乐器；它与 organ 最古老的义项重叠，但没有身体义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek tool-word, the real musical history and the real anatomical family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊工具词、真实的音乐史与真实的解剖词族。

normal.en: Greek organon meant tool; a body organ is the tool a body uses for a job.
normal.cn: 希腊 organon 意为工具；身体器官就是身体干活用的工具。

normal.en: The musical sense came first in English: organ meant the church instrument before it meant the body part.
normal.cn: 音乐义在英语中先出现：organ 先指教堂乐器，后指身体部件。

normal.en: Organelle is a little organ inside a cell; the suffix -elle marks the smaller scale.
normal.cn: organelle 是细胞里的小器官；后缀 -elle 标记更小的尺度。

normal.en: Official organ is the fixed phrase for a party newspaper, keeping the mouthpiece image.
normal.cn: official organ 是机关报的固定说法，保留了「喉舌」的意象。

normal.en: Vital organs, sense organs and reproductive organs name the function each set performs.
normal.cn: vital organs、sense organs、reproductive organs 都按各自执行的功能命名。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where every bench has one job and no bench does another's work.
abstract.cn: 想象一间作坊，每张工作台只做一道工序，绝不替别人干活。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe organ: many pipes, one instrument, each pipe responsible for one note.
abstract.cn: 想象一架管风琴：许多音管，一件乐器，每根管负责一个音。

abstract.en: Picture a newspaper as a mouth: the institution speaks through it the way a body speaks through a throat.
abstract.cn: 想象报纸是一张嘴：机构通过它发声，正如身体通过喉咙发声。

examples.en: The liver is an organ that removes toxins from the blood.
examples.cn: 肝脏是从血液中清除毒素的器官。

examples.en: The organ in the church was built in the eighteenth century.
examples.cn: 教堂里的管风琴建于 18 世纪。

examples.en: The committee is an organ of the local government.
examples.cn: 该委员会是地方政府的一个机关。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，干」（organ）——哦，干活（干）的就是器官与机构 → 器官；机构

root: 拉丁 organum，借自希腊 organon「工具、器具、乐器」，一般认为与 ergon「工作」相关；ergon 的印欧祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a part with a job: a body organ, a pipe organ, a state body, a party paper, vocal organs, sense organs, plant reproductive organs, and finally any instrument at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指「有专门职责的部件」：身体器官、管风琴、国家机关、机关报、发声器官、感觉器官、植物繁殖器官，最后泛指任何工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dedicated unit inside a larger machine, each unit doing one job.
core.cn: 核心意象：更大机器中的一个专职单元，每个单元只做一件事。

branches.en: BODY PARTS: voice, sense and reproductive parts each serve one function.
branches.cn: 身体部件：发声、感觉与繁殖部件各司一职。

branches.en: INSTRUMENT: a set of pipes, each with one job, becomes one musical organ.
branches.cn: 乐器：一组各司其职的音管，合成一件管风琴。

branches.en: PARTY VOICE: a newspaper speaks for a movement.
branches.cn: 党的喉舌：一份报纸替一场运动发声。

branches.en: THE OLD GENERAL SENSE: any tool or means, before the body and music senses narrowed the word.
branches.cn: 古老的泛义：在身体义与音乐义收窄词义之前，泛指任何工具或手段。

branches.en: ONE METAPHOR, TWO DOMAINS: body and state are both read as machines of specialised parts.
branches.cn: 一个比喻两个领域：身体与国家都被读作由专门部件组成的机器。

intro.en: Organ is a Greek loan that entered Latin, so its family mixes Greek suffixes with Latin and modern scientific endings.
intro.cn: organ 是经拉丁语进入的希腊借词，因此其词族混合了希腊后缀、拉丁后缀与现代科学词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin organum and Greek organikos give organic; Late Latin organizare gives organize and organization; New Latin organismus gives organism.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 organum 与希腊 organikos 衍生 organic；晚期拉丁 organizare 衍生 organize 与 organization；新拉丁 organismus 衍生 organism。

items.example: The Greek word named any instrument, including a musical one.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词泛指任何器具，包括乐器。

items.example: Latin medical texts used organum for body parts.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁医学文献用 organum 指身体部件。

items.structure: organum, shortened in French and English
items.example: Each organ in the abdomen has its own job.
items.exampleCN: 腹腔里的每个器官各有分工。

items.meaning: relating to organs or living things
items.example: Organic matter comes from living things.
A single cell can be a whole organism.
items.exampleCN: 单个细胞也可以是一个完整生物体。

items.meaningCN: 组织起来的机构或安排
items.example: The organization has offices in three cities.
items.exampleCN: 这个机构在三座城市设有办事处。

items.meaning: a small specialised part of a cell
items.meaningCN: 细胞内的小型专门结构
items.example: The mitochondrion is an organelle.

items.meaning: a person who plays the organ
items.example: The organist practised before the service.
items.exampleCN: 管风琴师在礼拜前练习。

items.meaning: a person who gives an organ for transplant
items.example: The register lists people willing to be an organ donor.
items.exampleCN: 登记册列出愿意捐献器官的人。

definition_zh: 有机的；与生物体有关的；含碳骨架的（化学）；不用化肥农药的（农业）；自然生长而成的
definition_en: relating to living things or to carbon-based compounds, and by extension grown without synthetic chemicals or developed naturally as a whole
core_image: 一棵植物从土壤里长出来，根、茎、叶彼此相连，整株像一件长成的器官而不是拼装的零件
scene: 这些蔬菜不用合成农药和可溶性化肥，摊位上挂着醒目的标签。Organic vegetables are grown without synthetic pesticides or soluble fertilizers.
sceneCN: 这里 organic 指「有机的（不用化肥农药的）」（第 3 个义项：农业上指以有机方式种植）；蔬菜不用合成农药与可溶化肥。图中可辨识物件：植物、土壤、根茎叶的连通、无化学瓶罐；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 有机食品；有机作物（作名词时多用于复数 organics，或 the organic 指有机农业）
有机的；生物体的；含碳的；有机耕作的；自然演成的

senses.title: Of living things
senses.definition: relating to living organisms or to the structures they build
senses.definitionCN: 与活生物或其构成的构造相关
senses.example: Soil organic matter feeds the whole food web.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤有机物养活了整个食物网。
senses.why: Greek organon named a tool, and a body's tools are its organs; 'organic' therefore starts as 'having organs', that is, belonging to a living body.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 organon 指工具，而身体的工具就是器官；因此 organic 起初意为「有器官的」，即属于活体。

senses.title: Carbon-based chemistry
senses.titleCN: 有机化学义：含碳骨架的化合物
senses.definition: describing compounds built on carbon skeletons, the chemistry once thought to require life
senses.definitionCN: 描述以碳骨架为基础的化合物，这一化学领域曾被以为只能由生命产生
senses.example: Methane is the simplest organic compound.
senses.exampleCN: 甲烷是最简单的有机化合物。
senses.why: because such compounds were first obtained only from living things, the word was carried over to the whole class even after they were synthesized in the lab.
senses.whyCN: 由于这类化合物最初只能从生物得到，即使后来能在实验室合成，这个词仍被沿用到整类物质上。

senses.title: Grown without synthetics
senses.titleCN: 农业义：不用化肥农药的
senses.definition: describing food grown without synthetic pesticides or soluble mineral fertilizers
senses.definitionCN: 描述不用合成农药或可溶矿物肥料的种植方式
senses.example: Organic apples cost more because the orchard yields less.
senses.exampleCN: 有机苹果更贵，因为果园产量更低。
senses.why: the farming sense borrows the idea of a whole living system, treating the soil as something to be fed rather than dosed.
senses.whyCN: 农业义借用「活着的整体系统」这一观念，把土壤当作需要喂养的东西，而不是投药的对象。

senses.title: Grown as a whole, not assembled
senses.titleCN: 演化义：自然生长、整体关联的
senses.definition: describing something that develops naturally as an interconnected whole rather than being assembled from parts
senses.definitionCN: 描述作为相互关联的整体自然发展，而非由零件拼装
senses.example: The firm's growth was organic, not the result of acquisitions.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司的增长是自然生长，而非并购的结果。
senses.why: since the body grows from within, 'organic' also means growth by inner development rather than by outside assembly, and business borrowed that.
senses.whyCN: 由于身体是从内部长成的，organic 也指由内在发展而非外部拼装的成长，商业领域借用了这一层。

senses.title: Of the organs in medicine
senses.definition: describing disease that has a structural change in an organ rather than a purely functional one
senses.definitionCN: 描述器官有结构改变、而非纯功能性的疾病
senses.example: The scan ruled out organic disease of the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描排除了胃的器质性病变。
senses.why: medicine must separate damage to an organ from symptoms without a lesion, so 'organic' marks the structural case.
senses.whyCN: 医学必须把器官的结构损伤与无病灶的症状分开，因此 organic 标记结构性的那一类。

senses.title: Parts that belong together
senses.titleCN: 结构义：组织上相互关联的
senses.definition: describing a structure whose parts are interdependent, like the organs of a body
senses.definitionCN: 描述各部分相互依赖的结构，如同身体的器官
senses.example: The report describes an organic link between the two agencies.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把两个机构之间的关系描述为有机联系。
senses.why: if organs serve one body, then any set of parts serving one end can be called organic.
senses.whyCN: 如果各器官服务于同一个身体，那么任何共赴一目的的一组部件都可以叫 organic。

senses.title: Foundational law and acts
senses.titleCN: 根本性义：作为根本法规的
senses.definition: describing a basic constitutional document or act, as in organic law
senses.definitionCN: 描述根本性的宪制文件或法令，如「组织法」
senses.example: The status of the territory is set by an organic act.
senses.exampleCN: 该领地的地位由一部组织法规定。
senses.why: a body needs a skeleton, so a state's founding instrument is called organic: it is what the rest is built onto.
senses.whyCN: 身体需要骨骼，因此国家的立国文件被称为「有机的」：其余一切都建在它之上。

senses.title: Whole food, whole system
senses.titleCN: 食品义：作为整体未被拆解的
senses.definition: describing food or a system treated as an intact whole rather than as isolated components
senses.definitionCN: 描述被当作完整整体、而非孤立成分处理的食品或系统
senses.example: The shop sells organics alongside conventional produce.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店把有机产品与常规农产品并排出售。
senses.why: the market turned the adjective into a noun, so 'organics' now names the goods themselves.
senses.whyCN: 市场把这个形容词变成名词，因此 organics 现在指商品本身。

intro.en: Organic comes from Greek organon 'tool, instrument', through Latin organum and the medieval adjective organicus. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: organic 出自希腊 organon「工具、器具」，经拉丁 organum 与中世纪形容词 organicus 而来。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: organon named a tool or instrument, and in philosophy a means of doing something. From it comes the sense of a body part that does work.
items.cn: organon 指工具或器具，也指哲学上达成某目的的手段。由它引申出「做工作的身体部件」这一义。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument and, in later use, a musical instrument; the body-part sense developed in anatomy.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具，后亦指乐器；身体部件的义项在解剖学中发展起来。

items.en: Medieval Latin organicus meant 'of an organ' or 'having organs'; English took the adjective in this anatomical sense first.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 organicus 意为「器官的」或「有器官的」；英语先在这个解剖学意义上使用该形容词。

items.en: Around 1800 chemists divided compounds into organic, from living things, and inorganic; urea's laboratory synthesis in 1828 weakened the boundary but the name stayed.
items.cn: 约 1800 年，化学家把化合物分为来自生物的 organic 与 inorganic；1828 年尿素在实验室被合成，动摇了这条界线，但名称保留。

items.en: The twentieth century applied the word to farming that avoids synthetic inputs, treating soil as a living system.
items.cn: 20 世纪把这个词用于避免合成投入物的耕作方式，把土壤当作活系统。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): organon's pre-Greek origin is not established, so any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：organon 在希腊语之前的来源并无定论，其背后的任何印欧形式都是重构，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek stem that name different things; group two holds words often used where organic could be chosen.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词干、但指不同事物的词；第二组是常与 organic 互换使用的词。

entries.definition: A part of a body or an organisation, not a quality; organic is the adjective describing such a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或机构的部件，不是性质；organic 是描述这类整体的形容词。

entries.definition: A complete living being; it shares organon but names an entity, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整的生物体；共享 organon，但命名实体而非性质。

entries.definition: A structured group of people, from the same stem via 'organize'. It names an institution, not a growing whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指有结构的人群，由同一词干经 organize 而来；命名机构，不是生长的整体。

entries.definition: Not built on carbon and not from life; it is the direct opposite in chemistry and farming.
entries.definitionCN: 不以碳为基础、非来自生命；在化学与农业中与 organic 直接相对。

entries.definition: Not made or altered by humans; organic in farming also implies natural methods, but natural says nothing about certification.
entries.definitionCN: 非人力制造或改动的；农业中的 organic 也含自然方式，但 natural 不涉及认证。

entries.definition: Relating to biology or to living processes; it names the science, while organic names a property of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物学或生命过程相关；命名学科，而 organic 命名物质属性。

entries.definition: Good for health or morally sound; organic food is often called wholesome, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 有益健康或品德端正；有机食品常被称 wholesome，但两词回答不同问题。

entries.definition: Arranged by an outside plan; organic growth is the opposite of planned assembly.
entries.definitionCN: 按外部方案安排；organic growth 恰与计划拼装相反。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek organon 'tool': a body's tools are its organs, so organic first means 'having organs'.
normal.cn: 希腊 organon「工具」：身体的工具就是器官，所以 organic 起初意为「有器官的」。

normal.en: The family runs organ, organism, organization, organic, organically, inorganic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 organ、organism、organization、organic、organically、inorganic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: organic matter, organic compound, organic farming, organic growth, organic chemistry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：有机物、有机化合物、有机农业、自然增长、有机化学。

normal.en: Chemistry pairs it with inorganic; farming pairs it with conventional.
normal.cn: 化学中与 inorganic 相对；农业中与常规耕作相对。

normal.en: The business sense is 'grown from within', the opposite of bought through acquisitions.
normal.cn: 商业义是「从内部长成」，与靠并购得来相反。

abstract.en: Picture a plant whose root, stem and leaf all serve one life.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物，根、茎、叶都服务于同一条生命。

abstract.en: Picture a city that grew along its roads instead of being stamped out at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市沿道路长出来，而不是一次压印成形。

abstract.en: Picture a table whose legs are not attached but grown from the same wood.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，桌腿不是装上去的，而是与桌面同一块木料长出来的。

examples.en: Organic matter in the soil holds water between grains.
examples.cn: 土壤中的有机物在颗粒之间持水。

examples.en: Organic chemistry began with compounds isolated from plants and animals.
examples.cn: 有机化学始于从动植物中分离出的化合物。

examples.en: The company preferred organic growth to borrowing for acquisitions.
examples.cn: 公司更愿自然增长，而不是借钱并购。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「有器官（organ）的」——凡活物长成的、含碳的、不用化肥的 → 有机的

root: 希腊 organon「工具、器具」→ 拉丁 organum → 中世纪拉丁 organicus「有器官的」→ 英语 organic；19 世纪扩展为化学义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: a body's parts all serve one life; that image is read as living matter, as carbon chemistry, as chemical-free farming, as growth from within, as structural disease, as interdependence, as a founding law, and as goods sold under that label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：身体的各部分都服务于同一条生命；这一意象依次被读成生命物质、碳化学、无合成投入的耕作、由内生长、器质性疾病、相互依赖、立国根本法，以及以此标签出售的商品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: root, stem and leaf all serving one living whole, with nothing bolted on.
core.cn: 核心意象：根、茎、叶都服务于同一个活的整体，没有一件是外装的。

branches.en: LIVING MATTER: the oldest sense, matter that belongs to a body.
branches.cn: 生命物质：最古老的义项，属于身体的物质。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: the carbon class, named when such compounds came only from life.
branches.cn: 化学：碳化合物这一类，命名时它们只来自生命。

branches.en: FARMING AND GOODS: soil fed as a living system, and produce sold as organics.
branches.cn: 农业与商品：把土壤当活系统来养，以及作为 organic 产品出售。

branches.en: GROWTH: development from within, borrowed by business for unplanned expansion.
branches.cn: 生长：由内发展，商业借指非计划性扩张。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: organ damage in medicine, interdependent parts, and a state's founding law.
branches.cn: 结构：医学上的器官损伤、相互依赖的部件，以及国家的立国根本法。

intro.en: Organic is Greek organon plus the Latin adjectival ending -icus, kept in English as -ic; the family also uses -ism and -ize.
intro.cn: organic 是希腊 organon 加拉丁形容词词尾 -icus，在英语中保留为 -ic；词族还用 -ism 与 -ize。

latinIntro.en: Latin organum is a borrowed Greek word, and medieval organicus is a Latin formation on it; both are real Latin, though the root is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 organum 是借自希腊语的词，中世纪 organicus 是在其上形成的拉丁词；二者都是真实的拉丁语，但词根属希腊语。

items.meaning: of organs, of living things; carbon-based
items.example: Organic waste can be composted.
The farm is organically certified.

items.meaning: a body part that does work
items.example: The liver is the largest internal organ.
items.exampleCN: 肝脏是最大的内部器官。

items.example: A single organism can be a whole forest patch.
items.exampleCN: 单个生物体可以是一整片林地。

items.example: The organization rewrote its charter.

items.meaningCN: 非碳基的、非来自生命的
items.example: Inorganic salts dissolve in the water.

items.meaning: dead or living material from organisms
items.meaningCN: 来自生物的活或死的物质
items.example: Organic matter improves soil texture.
Organic chemistry began with natural products.
items.exampleCN: 有机化学始于天然产物。

items.meaning: a small organ of a cell
items.example: The chloroplast is an organelle.

latinEntries.structure: organum, organi (n., second declension; Greek loanword)

definition_zh: 组织；机构；企业；编排；整理；组织结构
definition_en: a group of people with a particular purpose and structure, or the act of arranging things into an ordered system
core_image: 一张桌上摊开的机构图，方框之间用直线连成层级，没有一处悬空
scene: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处。The international organization keeps offices in three countries.
sceneCN: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处；句中的 organization 指「为特定目的而设立的机构」（第 2 个义项：机构、团体）。图中可辨识物件：机构图、办事处门牌、文件夹、地球仪；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 组织；机构；企业；编排；整理；组织结构

senses.title: A group with a purpose and a structure
senses.definition: a group of people working together with defined roles towards a shared aim
senses.definitionCN: 为共同目标而按既定角色协作的一群人
senses.example: Every organization needs someone to keep the records.
senses.exampleCN: 每个组织都需要有人保管记录。
senses.why: The word comes from the Greek word for a tool, and an organization is a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自希腊语中表示「工具」的词，组织就是为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

senses.title: An institution or body
senses.definition: an established body such as a charity, a union, a hospital or an international agency
senses.definitionCN: 已设立的机构，如慈善团体、工会、医院或国际机构
senses.example: The international organization keeps offices in three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织在三个国家设有办事处。
senses.why: Once a group acquires a name, rules and premises, it is spoken of as an institution rather than a gathering.
senses.whyCN: 当一群人有了名称、规则与办公场所，人们就说它是机构，而不只是一次聚会。

senses.title: A company treated as a body
senses.definition: a business viewed as a structured body of departments, staff and procedures
senses.definitionCN: 被视为由部门、人员与流程构成的企业
senses.example: The organization employs four hundred people across six sites.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业在六个地点雇了四百人。
senses.why: Calling a firm an organization shifts attention from its trade to its internal arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 把企业称作 organization，注意力就从它的买卖转到它的内部安排。

senses.title: The act of arranging something
senses.definition: the act of putting parts, events or tasks into a workable order
senses.definitionCN: 把各部分、活动或任务排成可运作次序的动作
senses.example: The organization of the festival took six months.
senses.exampleCN: 节庆的组织工作花了六个月。
senses.why: Before the word meant a body, it meant the act of giving parts an order, and that act still carries the name.
senses.whyCN: 在指团体之前，这个词指「给各部分定次序」的动作，这个动作至今仍用这个名称。

senses.title: The structure itself
senses.definition: the pattern of departments, ranks and reporting lines inside a body
senses.definitionCN: 机构内部部门、层级与汇报线的格局
senses.example: The new director redrew the organization within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管在一年内重画了组织结构。
senses.why: If organizing is giving order, the resulting order is also called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 如果组织是赋予次序，那么产生的次序也用同一个名称。

senses.title: The quality of being orderly
senses.definition: the quality of doing things in an ordered, planned way
senses.definitionCN: 以有序、有计划的方式做事的性质
senses.example: Her organization kept the whole project on schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 她的条理性让整个项目按计划推进。
senses.why: A person can possess the same order that a body has, so the noun also names a personal capacity.
senses.whyCN: 一个人也可以拥有团体那样的秩序，因此这个名词也指个人能力。

senses.title: The arrangement of living tissue
senses.definition: the structured arrangement of cells and tissues in a living body
senses.definitionCN: 活体中细胞与组织的结构安排
senses.example: The microscope revealed the organization of the leaf tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜显示出叶片组织的构造。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the word for the ordered arrangement of parts in a living thing, from the same tool image.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用这个词，指活体中各部分有序的安排，仍沿用「器具」的意象。

senses.title: An international body
senses.definition: a body set up by states or by agreement across borders to handle shared matters
senses.definitionCN: 由国家设立或跨国协议建立、处理共同事务的机构
senses.example: The organization was founded to coordinate relief after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国际组织是为协调战后救济而设立的。
senses.why: States needed permanent instruments for shared work, and the tool sense of the root fits that role exactly.
senses.whyCN: 各国需要为共同事务设立常设工具，词根的「器具」义正好契合这一角色。

intro.en: Organization comes from organize, built on Latin organum 'instrument', from Greek organon 'tool'. It first named the act of arranging and later the body so arranged. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: organization 来自 organize，其基础是拉丁 organum「器具」，再溯至希腊 organon「工具」。它先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。年代均为约数。

items.en: Organon meant 'tool, instrument', and Greek philosophy used it for an instrument of reasoning as well as a physical tool.
items.cn: organon 意为「工具、器具」，希腊哲学既用它指推理的工具，也指实物器具。

items.en: Latin borrowed organum for an instrument, and it also named a musical instrument and, later, a bodily organ.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 organum 指器具，也用来指乐器，后来又指身体器官。

items.en: The verb organize meant to give parts an order so that they work together, like fitting tools to a task.
items.cn: 动词 organize 意为给各部分定次序使它们协同运作，像把工具配到一项任务上。

items.en: In English organization first named the act of arranging; by the eighteenth century it named the body that results.
items.cn: 在英语中，organization 先指安排的动作；到十八世纪才指由此形成的团体。

items.en: Industrial and international bodies made the word the standard term for any structured group, from charities to agencies.
items.cn: 工业与国际机构使这个词成为任何有结构团体的标准称呼，从慈善团体到政府机构。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same organ root; group two holds words for structured groups.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「器具」词根的各种形式；第二组是表示有结构团体的词。

entries.definition: To arrange things or people into order; the act behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物或人排成次序；是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: A part of a body or a musical instrument, from the same tool word; it is not a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体器官或乐器，同出「器具」一词；不是团体。

entries.definition: An individual living being, whose parts are organized; it is a creature, not an institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个活体，其各部分有组织；是生物，不是机构。

entries.definition: Relating to an organization or its structure; it describes, while organization names.
entries.definitionCN: 与组织或其结构有关的形容词；描述性质，organization 命名实体。

entries.definition: An established body or custom with social standing; it stresses endurance, not internal arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指有社会地位的既定机构或惯例；强调持久，不强调内部安排。

entries.definition: A group of people joined for a shared interest, usually voluntarily; often smaller than an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 指为共同兴趣自愿结合的一群人；通常比 organization 小。

entries.definition: Any group treated as a unit, such as a governing body; it is vaguer about structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指被当作单位处理的任何群体，如管理机构；对结构说得更含糊。

entries.definition: A business, usually a professional partnership; it cannot name a charity or an agency.
entries.definitionCN: 指企业，通常是专业合伙；不能指慈善团体或政府机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Greek for tool: a group arranged like an instrument for a purpose.
normal.cn: 希腊语意为「工具」：为某个目的像器具一样被安排起来的一群人。

normal.en: The family runs organize, organization, organizational, organizer and organism.
normal.cn: 同族词有 organize、organization、organizational、organizer 与 organism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: a non-profit organization, an international organization, the organization of work.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各义项：非营利组织、国际组织、工作的安排。

normal.en: The same root gives organ, a body part that is itself a tool.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 organ，即本身就是「工具」的身体部件。

normal.en: The word first meant the act of arranging, then the body arranged.
normal.cn: 这个词先指安排的动作，后指被安排成的团体。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of boxes joined by straight lines, none of them floating.
abstract.cn: 想象一张方框图表，方框之间用直线相连，没有一个悬空。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox where every tool hangs in its own marked place.
abstract.cn: 想象一只工具箱，每件工具都挂在标好的位置上。

abstract.en: Picture a choir that breathes together without anyone shouting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，没人喊叫却一起换气。

examples.en: The organization trains volunteers to teach reading.
examples.cn: 这个组织培训志愿者教阅读。

examples.en: Poor organization wasted half the budget.
examples.cn: 糟糕的统筹浪费了一半预算。

examples.en: She is known for her organization and calm under pressure.
examples.cn: 她以有条理和临压不乱而出名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 方框用直线连成层级，没有一个悬空 → 组织

root: 拉丁 organum「器具」，来自希腊 organon「工具」；动词 organize 指给各部分定次序，organization 由「安排的动作」引申为「被安排成的团体与结构」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one instrument: the purposeful group, the institution, the company as a body, the act of arranging, the structure, the personal orderliness, the living tissue, and the international body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一件「器具」：有目的的团体、机构、作为组织看待的企业、安排的动作、组织结构、个人的条理性、活体组织，以及国际机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an instrument whose parts fit together so that it can do one job.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件器具，各部件互相咬合，从而能完成一项工作。

branches.en: GROUP AS TOOL: a purpose-driven group and a company seen as a body are the same instrument at different legal sizes.
branches.cn: 作为工具的群体：为目的一组人与被视为身体的企业，是同一器具的不同法律规模。

branches.en: LASTING BODY: a charity and an international agency are institutions built to keep working.
branches.cn: 持久的身体：慈善团体与国际机构都是为持续运作而建的机构。

branches.en: FITTING TOGETHER: before there is a body there is the act of giving parts an order.
branches.cn: 装配：在团体存在之前，先有给各部分定次序的动作。

branches.en: THE ORDER ITSELF: the pattern of departments and reporting lines is the result of arranging.
branches.cn: 次序本身：部门与汇报线的格局，是安排的结果。

branches.en: NATURAL ORDER: a tidy person and living tissue both show parts kept in working order.
branches.cn: 自然秩序：有条理的人与活体组织，都显示各部分保持运作秩序。

intro.en: Organization is a Greek tool word plus a Latin action suffix, a common pattern in academic English.
intro.cn: organization 是希腊语「工具」词加拉丁动作后缀，是学术英语中常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon passed into Latin as organum, giving organ, organize, organization and organism.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 organon 进入拉丁作 organum，给出 organ、organize、organization 与 organism。

items.example: The root pictures a tool fitted to a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘配到任务上的工具。

items.example: The word covered tools and organs alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词同时涵盖器具与器官。

items.example: The heart is an organ.
They organized the files by year.
items.exampleCN: 他们按年份整理了档案。

items.example: The organization keeps three offices.
items.exampleCN: 这个组织设有三个办事处。

items.example: The chart shows the organizational structure.
The organizer booked the hall.
A cell is part of an organism.
items.exampleCN: 细胞是生物体的一部分。

definition_zh: 组织；筹备；整理；编成团体；使有条理
definition_en: to plan and arrange an activity, to put things into order, to form people into a group or union, or to give separate parts a clear structure
core_image: 散落的零件被一双手按大小排好，一颗颗拧紧，装成一台能转动的机器
scene: 毕业典礼前一天的礼堂里，长桌上堆着没拆的纸箱，几个人来回比对清单，把椅子一排排摆好。They spent the afternoon organizing the chairs for the ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里的 organizing 是「组织、筹备」（第 1 个义项：筹划并安排一项活动）；句意为他们花了一下午为典礼摆放椅子。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、清单、成排的椅子。

pos.zh: 组织；筹备；整理；编成团体；使有条理

derivatives.zh: 由 organize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「组织；机构」
由 organize 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「组织者」
由 organization 加 -al 构成，义为「组织上的；机构的」

senses.title: To plan and arrange an activity or event
senses.definition: to make all the preparations needed for an activity or event, deciding who does what and when
senses.definitionCN: 为一项活动或事件做好全部准备，把谁做什么、何时做都安排妥当
senses.example: They spent the afternoon organizing the chairs for the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们花了一下午为典礼摆放椅子。
senses.why: The Greek source organon meant a tool, and the verb came to mean fitting parts together so that a whole can work, which is exactly what planning an event does.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头 organon 意为工具，这个动词后来指把各部分装配合用，使整体能够运转，而筹备一场活动做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To put things into a clear order
senses.definition: to arrange objects, papers or data so that they are easy to find and use
senses.definitionCN: 把物品、文件或资料排放妥当，使人容易查找和使用
senses.example: She organized her notes into three folders before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前她把笔记整理进三个文件夹。
senses.why: If a tool is a set of parts that fit, then a drawer or a folder can also be made to fit, so the same verb moves from machines to shelves and files.
senses.whyCN: 既然工具是一组彼此契合的部件，抽屉和文件夹也能被安排得彼此契合，于是同一个动词从机器走到了货架和文件。

senses.title: To form people into a group or union
senses.definition: to bring people together into a body with a shared purpose, such as a union or a team
senses.definitionCN: 把人们聚集起来，组成一个有共同目标的团体，如工会或队伍
senses.example: The workers organized a union in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在春天组织成立了一个工会。
senses.why: People, like parts, can be brought into a working arrangement, and when they act as one body the verb names the forming of that body.
senses.whyCN: 人和零件一样可以被装进一个能运转的安排里，当他们作为一个整体行动时，这个动词指的就是这个整体的形成。

senses.title: To arrange parts into a coherent whole
senses.definition: to give separate pieces of something, such as an essay or a plan, a logical and clear structure
senses.definitionCN: 给文章、方案等分散的部分安排出合乎逻辑而清晰的结构
senses.example: The report was poorly organized, so the main point was hard to find.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告编排得很乱，主旨很难找到。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is an instrument whose parts work together, and writing is organized when each paragraph has a job in the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最老的意思是各部件协同工作的器具，而文章之所以「有条理」，正是因为每段都在整体里担着一份职责。

intro.en: Organize came through medieval Latin from the Greek word for a tool; the tool image is the reason the verb can mean arranging parts, forming groups and giving a text a structure.
intro.cn: organize 经中世纪拉丁语上溯到希腊语中表示「工具」的词；正因为有这件工具的画面，这个动词才能表示装配部件、组成团体与安排文章结构。

items.en: Organon meant a tool or instrument, especially one made of parts that work together for a task.
items.cn: organon 意为工具、器具，尤指由若干协同工作的部件构成、用于某项任务的器具。

items.en: Latin took the word as organum, an instrument or a bodily organ, and also used it for a musical instrument.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词作 organum，指器具或身体器官，也用来指乐器。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed organizare, to organize or to give something its organs and parts, often used of the body and of a body of people.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出 organizare，意为组织、赋予某物器官与部件，常用于身体，也用于一群人构成的团体。

items.en: French took the verb as organiser, meaning to arrange or to set up, and English borrowed it in the same practical sense.
items.cn: 法语把该动词作 organiser，意为安排、设立，英语借入时也带着同样实用的意味。

items.en: Modern English keeps organize for events, for shelves and files, for unions and teams, and for the structure of writing or plans.
items.cn: 现代英语让 organize 兼指活动筹备、货架与文件的整理、工会与队伍的组织，以及文章或方案的结构安排。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Greek and Latin stem for tool and organ; the near-meaning group collects verbs for putting things into order.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在希腊语与拉丁语「工具、器官」词干上的词；近义组收表示「把事物安排有序」的动词。

entries.definition: A part of the body with a special job, or a large musical instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 身体中担负特定功能的部位，或大型乐器。

entries.definition: Relating to living things, or grown without artificial chemicals.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物有关的，或不用人工化学物质种植的。

entries.definition: The act of arranging, or a group that has been arranged.
entries.definitionCN: 安排的行为，或被组织起来的团体。

entries.definition: A person who plans and arranges an event.
entries.definitionCN: 筹划并安排活动的人。

entries.definition: To put things in a particular order or position.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物按某种次序或位置放好。

entries.definition: To make different parts work together smoothly.
entries.definitionCN: 使不同部分顺畅地配合运作。

entries.definition: To separate things into groups by type.
entries.definitionCN: 按种类把事物分成组。

entries.definition: To put things into named categories.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物归入有名目的类别。

normalIntro.en: Organize rests on the Greek word for a tool, so its hooks keep the picture of separate parts being fitted into something that works.
normalIntro.cn: organize 建立在希腊语表示「工具」的词上，所以记忆钩子始终保留「分散的部件被装成一件能用的东西」的画面。

normal.en: The Greek word organon is a tool, and an organ in the body is a tool of that organ's own kind, which is why the family keeps the sense of parts that work.
normal.cn: 希腊语 organon 是工具，而身体里的器官正是各自那一类的工具，所以这一族词始终带着「部件在起作用」的意味。

normal.en: Organize ends in -ize, the verb ending that means to make or to put into a state, so to organize is to make something into an ordered body.
normal.cn: organize 以 -ize 收尾，这个动词词尾表示「使成为某种状态」，所以组织就是把某物变成一个有序的整体。

normal.en: Organization is organize plus -ation, the ending that names an action or its result, so the same stem gives both the act and the body.
normal.cn: organization 是 organize 加 -ation，这个后缀指行为或其结果，所以同一个词干既给出动作，也给出团体。

normal.en: Organize a meeting and organize information share one verb because both put scattered pieces into a workable order.
normal.cn: organize a meeting 与 organize information 共用一个动词，因为两者都把零散的东西排成可用的次序。

normal.en: Note the British spelling with s and the American spelling with z, just as organisation and organization differ.
normal.cn: 留意英式拼写用 s、美式拼写用 z，正如 organisation 与 organization 的差别。

abstract.en: A word that began with a tool reminds us that order is not decoration; it is what makes separate parts able to do something together.
abstract.cn: 一个从工具起步的词提醒人：秩序不是装饰，而是让分散部件能一起做成一件事的条件。

abstract.en: To organize people is to treat them as parts of one body, which is powerful and also a little dangerous.
abstract.cn: 把人组织起来，就是把他们当作一个整体的部件，这既有力量，也带一点危险。

abstract.en: Every tidy shelf and every clear paragraph is the same small victory over scatter.
abstract.cn: 每一个整齐的货架、每一段清晰的文字，都是对「散乱」的同一场小小胜利。

examples.en: They spent the afternoon organizing the chairs for the ceremony.
examples.cn: 他们花了一下午为典礼摆放椅子。

examples.en: She organized her notes into three folders.
examples.cn: 她把笔记整理进三个文件夹。

examples.en: The workers organized a union in the spring.
examples.cn: 工人们在春天组织成立了一个工会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，搁那儿整」——东西都搁在那儿，一件件整好；记住 organize 是整理、组织。

sensesIntro.en: The core is parts fitted into a working whole; the senses divide by what is fitted together, an event, a set of objects, a group of people, or the pieces of a text.
